prompts.prompt: A 250ml glass bottle labeled 'Kaapi Cold' cold brew coffee stands upright on a wet dark slate surface, heavily beaded with condensation, surrounded by scattered ice cubes catching cool blue-white light. Soft frosty mist drifts across the frame. Camera does a slow 180-degree orbit around the bottle at eye level, background is a soft bokeh of green coffee cherries and water droplets on a dark teal backdrop. Realistic macro product cinematography, crisp highlights on the glass, refreshing and premium mood. No people, no hands, just the product. Vertical 9:16 framing. Sound design: gentle lo-fi chill ambient bed, subtle ice-clink foley, soft low whoosh as camera moves — no dialogue, no voiceover.

Cold brew coffee pours in slow motion from the Kaapi Cold bottle into a tall glass packed with ice, rich dark liquid swirling and splashing, condensation glistening under cool blue studio light. Camera pushes in tight on the pour, then pulls back to reveal the bottle and glass side by side on the slate surface with soft steam-like cold mist rolling across the table, ending on a clean hero shot with the 'Kaapi Cold' label sharp and legible, small on-screen text fades in: 'Chilled. Fresh. Kaapi Cold.' No people, no hands, product only. Vertical 9:16 framing. Sound design: satisfying pour and splash foley, ice clinking, a short bright chime as text appears — no dialogue, no voiceover.

notes: Scene 2 is riskiest: fluid pour/splash physics and keeping the label crisp and readable while liquid is in motion are the hardest things for Veo to render convincingly — expect to regenerate a few takes and pick the cleanest splash timing. Since no product photos were provided, generate and approve a still for each scene first (bottle-only hero still for Scene 1, pour/glass still for Scene 2) before running image-to-video, so the label design and bottle shape stay consistent across both clips. Final edit: trim/blend both 8s clips to a tight 15s cut for Reels, add a short brand-color end card if needed.
